summary: Iteration 4 backend testing for Spark dating app: Resend graceful failure on placeholder key, Profile Boost (POST/GET /api/me/boost + /status with weekly limits 1 premium / 3 VIP), Profile Viewers (POST /api/profile/view/{id} idempotent within 1 hour + GET /api/me/viewers premium-only), and Undo Swipe (premium-only, deletes swipe + cleans match). 17/17 tests in /app/backend/tests/test_iteration4.py PASSED. Resend errors are caught and logged as WARNING (no traceback), tickets persisted to db.support_tickets and db.bug_reports with deliver_to=support@sparkmatch.dating. VIP 4x boost call correctly returns 429. /api/me/viewers does NOT collide with /api/profile/{id} route (no 'User not found' error). Discover correctly sorts boosted profiles first and exposes is_boosted boolean.

minor.issue: The 'restore swipe count' branch (lines 681-685) is dead code — it checks `subscription == 'free'` but the earlier gate at line 663 already 402s free users. As a result, undo never restores daily_swipes_remaining for anyone. Since premium users have unlimited swipes (no decrement in /api/swipe), this is currently harmless, but the intent in spec ('restores count') is not implemented for the case where a premium user might be downgraded to free later.

Sort key is (not boost_active, last_active) with reverse=False — last_active strings end up sorted ASCENDING (oldest first). Boosted-first ordering works, but among non-boosted profiles the oldest last_active wins, which is the opposite of the intended 'most recently active first'.
Free users get weekly_limit=0 (correct) but no premium_required hint. Not a bug per spec; just noting.

action_items: Consider removing dead code in /api/swipe/undo lines 681-685 (the `if user.get('subscription') == 'free':` branch can never execute because of the 402 gate above) OR move the gate after the count-restore so a future downgrade-from-premium scenario is handled.

Discover sort: `profiles.sort(key=lambda p: (not boost_active(p), p.get('last_active') or ''), reverse=False)` sorts last_active ASCENDING. To get boosted-first then most-recently-active, use a negative-string trick or split into two sorted lists.
server.py is now 1694 lines (was 1514) — continue tracking the >700 split recommendation (boost/viewers/undo/support routers).
Resend integration: confirmed graceful — `send_email` catches Exception and `asyncio.create_task` ensures non-blocking. When a real RESEND_API_KEY is provided, no code change is needed.
critical_code_review_comments: Dead branch in undo_swipe: lines 681-685 unreachable due to 402 gate at line 663-664.
Boost rate-limit uses `db.boost_events.count_documents` with $gte on ISO string — works because ISO 8601 lexical order == chronological order, but a tz-aware index would be more explicit.
/api/me/viewers $group aggregation uses `$first` on already-sorted-DESC pipeline so last_viewed_at is correct. Good. But there's no pagination — capped at 100 viewers hard-coded.
send_email returns None on placeholder key but doesn't expose any signal to the caller — tickets must rely solely on DB persistence to know they're 'received', which works.
/api/profile/view/{target_user_id} does NOT validate that target_user_id exists in db.users — a malicious client could spam profile_views with junk IDs. Add an existence check or unique index.
Discover ASCENDING last_active sort (see action items).
